citation.title: Generative Design by Reinforcement Learning: Enhancing the Diversity of Topology Optimization Designs
citation.authors: Seowoo Jang; Soyoung Yoo; Namwoo Kang
citation.version_coded: arXiv v2 (16 February 2021), latest accessible full text; published 2022

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The neural wheel-design surrogate produces a topology in milliseconds of inference, whereas the iterative classical optimizer generally takes about 10 minutes.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 3 gives ~10 min classical and <10 ms neural inference: 600 s / 0.01 s = >60,000×, reported here as a lower bound of 60,000. Section 5 says 'order of milliseconds' without a precise value.
claim.alternatives: Abstract makes qualitative CPU-versus-GPU speed claim. Section 4.3 compares GDNet diversity with greedy, equal-distance, and exhaustive parameter search; exhaustive search takes ~4 h.

baseline.classical_method: Iterative multiobjective wheel topology optimization of Oh et al. (2019), minimizing compliance and distance to a reference design under a volume constraint (Section 3.1)
baseline.implementation: CPU algorithm; software details not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: CPU, model not stated (abstract and Section 3.5)
baseline.problem_size: 128 × 128 output images (Section 3.3); FE mesh and DOF count not stated
baseline.classical_time: order of 10 min per wheel design (Section 3; Section 5)
baseline.ml_time: <10 ms inference (Section 3); <1 ms GPU job in Section 3.5
baseline.data_generation_cost: 639 reference images × 121 optimizer runs each = 77,319 optimization outputs [inferred from Section 3.2]; wall-clock generation cost not stated
baseline.quality_metric: image cross entropy, pixel difference, IoU, and compliance MAPE relative to classical-generated designs (Section 3.5, Table 1); diversity and compliance for GDNet (Section 4.3, Figure 18)
baseline.quality_gap: not stated as a direct matched-quality gap for the speed claim; Section 3.5 Table 1 reports nonzero error metrics versus classical output

R1.evidence: Sections 3 and 5: neural inference is compared with a classical full optimization run; Section 3.5 reports similarity and compliance error but no same-quality or equal-time comparison for the speed claim.

R2.evidence: Abstract and Section 3.5: CPU classical optimization is compared with GTX 1080 Ti GPU inference without justification; Section 3.3 gives image resolution, not FE DOFs, so R2(c) is not established.

R3.evidence: Sections 3.2 and 5: many classical optimizer outputs are generated for learning, but no wall-clock data-generation or training cost and no break-even count accompany the inference speed claim.

R4.evidence: Section 3.5 and Figure 18: compliance of generated designs is evaluated alongside image/diversity measures, but volume/constraint violation and failed-design rates are not reported.

notes: The queue's 2020 title matches arXiv v1; arXiv v2 has a revised title, one additional author, and a later journal version. No open version-of-record full text was located. The size 128 × 128 is an output image, not evidence of FE degrees of freedom.
